candidates.exact_claim: The step-j Householder support is I_j={j+1,...,min(j+r+1,n)}; it removes the active column bulge, leaves earlier columns intact, and confines newly created below-subdiagonal entries to rows through j+r+2. The product Q also preserves the initial direction.
candidates.why_warranted: The proof tracks a moving active support and a Hessenberg zero band across consecutive two-sided updates. A small sparsity-pattern sequence would make which rows and columns change, where the bulge moves, and how it exits the last column immediately checkable.
candidates.specific_content: Show a banded matrix with the Hessenberg band, one active bulge at column j, the row/column support I_j for P_j, and the resulting active column after annihilation; include one next-step frame and the terminal n<=2 / j=n-2 boundary case. Mark unchanged columns k<j. Keep indices consistent with the source one-based convention and distinguish r=1 from r=2.

candidates.exact_claim: Periodic inputs are converted to open-boundary TT; single-site or adjacent two-site windows are visited in forward then reverse order, with left/right canonical QR environments and an SVD split after two-site updates.
candidates.why_warranted: This is a long algorithm whose main geometric structure is the movement of one- or two-site active windows while left and right isometric environments are maintained. A sweep diagram would clarify window order, center embedding, and direction-dependent SVD absorption.
candidates.specific_content: Draw TT cores as boxes joined by bond indices; shade the active one-site/two-site window; mark left-isometric and right-isometric environments; show forward arrows left-to-right and backward arrows right-to-left. For two sites, show reshape X=UΣV* and the forward U / ΣV* versus backward UΣ / V* absorption. Label the optional rank-capped rounding only after a complete forward/backward sweep.
